verdict.rationale: PagerDuty documents user-configurable background automations. Incident Workflows use trigger/action "if-this-then-that" logic and can fire automatically for all P1 and P2 incidents. Event Orchestration deduplicates or suppresses alerts automatically, and agentic features such as the Shift Agent coordinate schedule changes "without manual intervention". Missing for 10: independent or hands-on corroboration that these automations run reliably unattended, and deeper documentation of how users configure autonomous agent behavior (e.g. SRE Agent autonomy limits).

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can set up automations that run autonomously in the background

citations.quote: Incident Workflows allow you to build an automated response for every incident. For example, you can configure one workflow that automatically triggers for all P1 and P2 incidents
Through highly-configurable triggers and actions, you can apply "if-this-then-that" logic to orchestrate the right response for your teams, processes, and business.
Event Orchestration: Automatically deduplicate or suppress alerts.
monitors calendars, detects potential conflicts, identifies qualified replacements, and coordinates schedule changes without manual intervention
users can configure Skills to arm the SRE Agent with instructions, scripts, and resources that give it specialized capabilities and domain expertise
